newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three coalition leaders have pressed the prime minister to act against the attorney-general over the Bangkok Bank of Commerce controversy. PM Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, however, does not respond to demands for action against Kanit na Nakhon. Meanwhile, the attorney-general has issued an interim order allowing special public prosecutors' committees to decide on cases without having to refer to him for a final say. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The Constitution Drafting Committee's proposal to allow for an unelected prime minister has drawn strident opposition from Uthai Pimchaichon, who leads the political reform process. Uthai, who chairs the Constitution Drafting Assembly, says the country should have learned a lesson from the tenures of Thanom Kittikachorn and Kriangsak Chomanand, who were unelected. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Cabinet has approved a 4.56-billion baht budget for 2,500 scholarships for overseas studies in a long-term plan to combat brain drain and create efficient government officials. The scholarships, to be granted from next year to 2002, are the first half of a 10-year plan proposed by the Office of Civil Service Commission. The budget for the second half of the plan - an equal number of scholarships to be offered from 2003 to 2007 - will be decided after evaluating the first half. (THE NATION)

- Three panels have been set up by the board of directors of New Bangkok International Airport to work out the modalities involving the second Bangkok international airport. However, permanent secretary for Finance says the board has agreed that the project must go ahead without being relocated. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thailand's sugar industry could plunge into crisis next year if measures are not put into place to cushion the impact of falling world sugar prices. World sugar supply will soon outpace consumption, topping out at the same time as stockpiles peaked. The excess supply is expected to push the world sugar price down below 10 cents U.S. per pound. (BANGKOK POST)

- More than 10 Thai-owned garment factories in Laos have moved out of the country, which is facing increased competition from Cambodia. An executive member of Thai Garment Manufacturers Association says only two or three of the 14 factories in Laos are still operating while the rest have moved out because of the lack of business, unskilled labour and raw materials. (THE NATION)
